# @dpup/meshcore-mcp

> A Model Context Protocol server that exposes a MeshCore node — and the mesh
> reachable through it — as a clean, high-signal interface for any AI agent or
> tool. It wraps a @dpup/meshcore-ts MeshCoreClient behind a small, deliberately
> shaped surface of MCP tools, resources, and prompts: structured, digested
> results instead of raw frames. ESM-only, Node ≥ 18. The device layer, ungated
> by design — no policy, no admin-channel gate, no autonomous behavior.

`meshcore-mcp` is a thin server wedged between two contracts it does not own: the
MCP protocol above (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk's `McpServer`) and the
@dpup/meshcore-ts `MeshCoreClient` below. `MeshService` is the device-facing
core; it takes its `MeshCoreClient` and a `Clock` by injection, so the same code
runs against a real radio in production (`MeshCoreClient.tcp(host, port)` +
`SystemClock`) and a @dpup/meshcore-sim `SimConnection` + `SimClock` in tests —
nothing below `MeshService` can tell which. The primary consumer is a human
operator with Claude Code: add one `mcpServers` entry pointing at a node
(`MESHCORE_HOST`/`MESHCORE_PORT`, or `MESHCORE_SERIAL_PATH`) and operate the mesh
in natural language. Embedders call `createServer({ service })`.

## Tools

- `get_node_health(node?)`: Consolidated health snapshot — identity, radio, battery, uptime/queue, stats. Omit `node` for the home node; a name/hex prefix for a remote. Hides home-vs-remote and any remote login. read-only, idempotent.
- `survey_mesh()`: Roster of the home node and every known contact, with role and last-heard time. read-only, idempotent.
- `get_recent_traffic(since?)`: Recent live traffic from the rolling buffer, oldest→newest, each tagged with structural provenance. `since` is ISO-8601 or epoch-ms. read-only, idempotent.
- `send_message(target, text)`: Transmit to a contact (name/hex prefix) or channel (`#name`, `#index`, bare index). Action; NOT idempotent — a resend is a second transmission.
- `admin(node, command, params?, dryRun?)`: Run one enumerated admin command, home or remote (collapses the `login → CliData → reply` handshake). `dryRun: true` previews intent without contacting the device. Statically destructive; the per-command risk tier is in the result. `command` is an enumerated, curated set of 16 — never free-form.

## Resources

- `meshcore://traffic/live`: Subscribable. Inbound mesh events; the server pushes `notifications/resources/updated`, the client re-reads to fetch. Every event carries provenance — sender, channel identity, and a structural `decryptVerified` boolean (verified `channelMessage`/`contactMessage` vs. unverified `channelData`/`advert`/`raw`).
- `meshcore://nodes`: Pull-style roster — the home device plus every known contact, with role and last-heard time.
- `meshcore://contacts`: Pull-style contact list — name, public key, role, location, last-heard.

## Prompts

- `morning-mesh-check`: A daily health sweep — survey, flag quiet nodes, spot-check the suspicious ones.
- `diagnose-quiet-node(node)`: Work out why a node has gone quiet — health, recent traffic, last-heard, context.
- `draft-outage-notice(node, window?)`: Draft a concise outage notice over a window, and send it on approval.

## Docs

- [API reference](https://github.com/dpup/meshcore-mcp/blob/main/docs/api.md): Complete, generated reference — every exported symbol with full signatures and types. Source of truth.
- [Guide](https://github.com/dpup/meshcore-mcp/blob/main/docs/guide.md): Concepts and recipes — configuring the home node, the tool surface & annotations, the live stream & provenance, the `admin` set & dry-run, the three consumers, and testing your own agent against a sim-backed server.
- [README](https://github.com/dpup/meshcore-mcp/blob/main/README.md): Overview, the Claude Code MCP-config snippet, the tool/resource/prompt tables, install, the sim-backed quickstart, and design philosophy.

## Examples

- [demo](https://github.com/dpup/meshcore-mcp/blob/main/examples/demo.ts): A guided tour — an in-memory MCP `Client` against the real server over a sim-backed `MeshCoreClient`: tools (home + an offline repeater failing cleanly), the live stream with verified vs. unverified provenance, and `admin` dry-run then a scripted exec. Run with: `bun examples/demo.ts [--seed <n>]`.

## Notes

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/dpup/meshcore-mcp/blob/main/AGENTS.md): Architecture, the two contracts, the provenance mapping, the layout (config.ts, service/*, tools/*, resources/*, prompts/*), conventions, and the don't-regress list.
- The reference (docs/api.md) is generated by `bun run docs` and CI-verified to stay in sync with the source (`bun run docs:check`); treat it as authoritative over any prose.
- Two contracts: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk above, @dpup/meshcore-ts below — `meshcore-mcp` owns neither.
- The injected `Clock` is a design rule (no raw `Date.now()`/`setTimeout` below the entrypoint); provenance is structural (verified vs. unverified is derived from which event fired, not a wire flag); `admin` is enumerated, never free-form.
